source: Figma MCP reads (get_metadata, get_design_context, get_variable_defs, get_screenshot) of the Core Component file.

use_when: To trigger a primary action, such as submitting a form or confirming a choice.
When the action is a single, clear next step the user should take.
For calls-to-action that need visual emphasis — use the filled/primary style.
For secondary or less prominent actions — use the outline style instead of a second filled button.
To open a modal, drawer, or another view, when the action is not a navigation link.
For destructive actions (e.g. delete, remove), paired with the error/danger state.
Inside forms, toolbars, cards, and dialogs — wherever a discrete, tappable action is needed.
dont_use_when: For navigation between pages or views — use a Link component instead.
When more than one primary action competes for attention on the same screen — keep only one primary button per view.
As a label or static status indicator — use a Badge/Lozenge component instead.
For a toggleable on/off state — use a Toggle or Checkbox component instead.
best_practice: Use clear, action-oriented labels (e.g. "Save changes", not "OK").
Keep a single primary (filled) button per screen or section; make all other actions secondary/outline.
Always design a hover and error/disabled state so users get feedback on interaction.
Don't stack more than two buttons side by side without a clear visual hierarchy.
Keep button labels to 1–3 words; avoid full sentences.
Reserve the error/outline-error state for destructive or blocking actions only.
Keep a minimum 40px tap target height for touch interfaces.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame lays out state (rows) against StartIcon: True / False (columns), once with EndIcon: True and once with EndIcon: False.

themes.note: The Button page renders every cell in one theme. There is no dark-mode frame on the page.

Avatar.description: Shows a person's profile photo in a circle. size: sm 24px (default; dense lists, inline with text), md 30px (the header avatar), lg 40px (profiles, message threads). Drop the photo onto the photo layer; it fills and crops to the circle.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame lays the three sizes out in one row, sm 24x24, md 30x30 and lg 40x40, each labelled.

themes.note: The Avatar frame renders every size once, on the dark overlay background (--color-bg-overlay). It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To show the signed-in user's profile photo, such as in the header.
To represent a person (a host, guest or reviewer) next to their name or content.
Use md (30px) in the header, sm (24px) in dense lists or inline with text, and lg (40px) where the person is the focus, such as a profile or message thread.
dont_use_when: For brand or company logos: use the Logo component instead.
For listing or content photos: use the Image component instead.
As a clickable control on its own: place it inside a Button or Link so it has an accessible name.
best_practice: Crop photos square with the face centred; the circle clips the corners.
Keep one avatar size within the same list or row.
Give the image alt text with the person's name, or leave it empty when the name is shown right beside it.
Use only the sm, md and lg sizes; don't scale an avatar to other sizes.
Always supply a photo. There's no fallback for a missing photo yet.

Checkbox.description: Lets the user turn one option on or off, or confirm something before continuing. state: unchecked (default), checked, error (acknowledging a destructive action). Properties: Label (text), ShowLabel (show or hide). The tick shows the checked state, so it doesn't rely on colour alone.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (109:485) lays out state (rows: unchecked, checked) against ShowLabel (columns: True, False). The component set (117:23) publishes two variants, state=unchecked (117:12) and state=checked (117:15). Label (text, default "Label") and ShowLabel are component properties. The error state is named in the component description but is not drawn.

themes.note: The Checkbox frame renders every cell in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

unboundValues.property: gap between the box and the label

use_when: To let the user opt in to something, such as marketing emails or staying signed in.
To confirm the user has read and agreed to terms before they continue, such as the booking terms or cancellation policy.
To make the user acknowledge a destructive action before it runs, using the error state (for example, "I understand this is permanent").
For a list of options where the user can choose any number, such as search filters.
dont_use_when: For a setting that takes effect immediately: use the Toggle component instead.
When the user must pick exactly one option from a list: use the Radiocard component instead.
To trigger an action: use the Button component instead.
best_practice: Always give the checkbox a visible label that says what ticking it does.
Write labels as positive statements ("Email me deals"), not negatives ("Don't email me").
Leave opt-in checkboxes unticked by default.
Make the whole label clickable, not just the 16px box.
Use the error state only for acknowledging destructive or irreversible actions.
Put extra detail in helper text below the label, not in the label itself.

Chip.description: A selectable pill for filtering results or switching category. state: unselected (default), selected (blue, a filter that's on), selected-strong (navy, the active category in a category row). Property: Label. One size, 32px high.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (122:2) lays the three states out in one column, each beside a text label (unselected, selected, selected-strong). The component set (121:15) publishes three variants, state=unselected (121:8), state=selected (121:11) and state=selected-strong (121:13). Label (text, default "Label") is a component property, not a matrix axis. Every variant is 64x32 with the default label.

themes.note: The Chip frame renders every state once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To filter a list of results, such as search filters ("Pool", "Pet friendly", "Free cancellation").
To switch between categories of the same content, such as "All", "Bedrooms" or "Kitchen" in a photo gallery.
Use the selected state (blue) for filters the user has turned on, and selected-strong (navy) for the active category in a category row.
To show how many items an option holds, as part of the label (for example, "Kitchen 6").
dont_use_when: To show a status such as "Confirmed" or "Pending": use a Badge component instead.
To trigger an action, such as booking or submitting: use the Button component instead.
For a yes or no choice inside a form: use the Checkbox component instead.
To go to another page: use the Link component instead.
best_practice: Keep labels short: one to three words, plus an optional count.
A chip that's on must use a selected state, so the current selection is always visible.
Don't mix selected and selected-strong chips in the same row.
Space chips 8px apart in one row; let the row scroll or wrap on small screens rather than shrinking the chips.
When several filters can be on at once, give the user a way to clear them all.
Mark the selected chip for assistive technology (aria-pressed or aria-selected), not with colour alone.

Image.description: A photo in a fixed aspect ratio. ratio: 4:3 (default), 1:1, 3:2, 16:9, 2:1. radius: none (default; edge to edge inside a card), sm 6px (thumbnails), md 12px (standalone photos). The ratio is locked, so resize by width. Drop the photo onto the photo layer; it fills and crops to the frame.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (124:2) lays out ratio (rows: 4:3, 1:1, 3:2, 16:9, 2:1) against radius (columns: none, sm, md). The component set (123:22) publishes all 15 variants, named ratio=4:3, radius=none through ratio=2:1, radius=md. Figma draws no states.

themes.note: The Image frame renders every cell in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To show a photo of a listing, room or place, such as the photo at the top of a property card or the photos in a listing gallery.
Use radius none for a photo that runs edge to edge inside a card; the card rounds the corners.
Use radius md (12px) for standalone photos such as the gallery and marketing tiles, and radius sm (6px) for small thumbnails in lists.
Use 16:9 for wide gallery and hero photos, 3:2 for property cards, 4:3 or 1:1 for thumbnails, and 2:1 for banners and marketing tiles.
dont_use_when: For a person's profile photo: use the Avatar component instead.
For the Horizon Stays brand mark: use the Logo component instead.
For icons or small symbols: use an icon from the Icon Library instead.
best_practice: Choose the ratio first, then resize by width; the ratio is locked, so photos never stretch.
Crop the photo to fill the frame; don't letterbox or distort it.
Keep one ratio and radius across a group, such as every card in a results list.
Give every meaningful image alt text that describes it; leave alt text empty for purely decorative images.
Show the placeholder while a photo loads, in the same ratio, so the layout doesn't jump.

Link.description: Text that takes the user to another page or runs a secondary action. size: md 13px (default), sm 12px (dense rows, beside filters). state: default, hover (underlined). Property: Label. Medium weight in color/text/link.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (134:2) lays out state (rows: default, hover) against size (columns: md, sm). The component set (133:12) publishes all 4 variants, named size=md, state=default (133:4), size=md, state=hover (133:6), size=sm, state=default (133:8) and size=sm, state=hover (133:10). Label (text, default "Link") is a component property, not a matrix axis. Figma draws no focus, visited or disabled variants.

themes.note: The Link frame renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To take the user to another page or view, such as "Show all 24 amenities" or "Forgot your password?".
For a secondary action next to a form, such as "Resend code" or "Use a different email address".
To edit or manage an item in a list, such as "Edit" or "Manage" in account settings.
Use size md (13px) next to body text and on its own, and size sm (12px) in dense rows, such as "Clear" beside filters.
dont_use_when: For the main action on a page, such as submitting a form or booking: use the Button component instead.
To filter results or switch categories: use the Chip component instead.
To open a list of options to choose from: use the Dropdown component instead.
best_practice: Write link text that says where it goes or what it does ("Show all 24 amenities"), never "click here".
Keep links short, usually one to five words.
Underline a link that sits inside a sentence of body text, so it doesn't rely on colour alone; standalone links can use the default style.
Use the same link text for the same destination everywhere.
Leave space or a separator between two links next to each other.
Make sure every link shows a visible keyboard focus style.

Logo.description: The Horizon Stays logo. type: lockup (default; mark and wordmark, the header logo), mark (the icon alone). 32px high, vector. Brand colours are fixed on purpose and don't follow UI tokens: mark #3B82F6 with white, wordmark #2e7cc4.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (137:18) lays the two variants out in one column, each beside a text label. The component set (137:17) publishes two variants, type=lockup (137:6, 162x32) and type=mark (137:12, 32x32). Figma draws no states and no sizes.

themes.note: The Logo frame renders both variants once, in one theme, and has no separate light and dark frames. The mark is the committed SVG asset (src/assets/images/logo-mark.svg) with its colours fixed inside the file, and the wordmark colour is a fixed literal in the stylesheet, so neither follows the UI theme tokens and the Logo does not change between light and dark. Figma's Best Practice says there's no version for dark backgrounds yet.

unboundValues.property: fill colours inside the vector: tile #3B82F6, sun and wave white
unboundValues.codeNote: Set inside the SVG asset, not in the stylesheet

use_when: At the left of the header on every page, using the lockup at 32px high.
Use the mark on its own where there's no room for the wordmark, such as a collapsed sidebar, an app icon or a favicon.
dont_use_when: For listing, room or place photos: use the Image component instead.
For a person's profile photo: use the Avatar component instead.
As a decorative icon or bullet: use an icon from the Icon Library instead.
best_practice: Use the logo as it is: don't recolour, stretch, rotate or add effects to it.
Scale an instance proportionally only (hold Shift while resizing); never change its width and height separately.
Don't edit the wordmark text or retype it in another font.
Leave clear space around the logo; don't crowd it with other elements.
Place it on a light background so the blue stays readable; there's no version for dark backgrounds yet.
Don't show the mark and the lockup side by side on the same screen.
